title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (9) 'Une conjecture arithmético-géométrique' (begun on p.28). M_{g,ν} is the moduli stack over Q of smooth proper curves of genus g with ν ordered disjoint sections. M̄_{g,ν} is its geometric version over Q̄. The stack is hyperbolic except for (g,ν) = (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0), the exceptions recalled in the top-left margin. Fix a geometric point ξ, corresponding to a curve (X; x_1,…,x_ν) over Q̄. There is an outer action of π_1(M_{g,ν},ξ) on the profinite group π̂ = π_1(X∖{x_i})^. Its image lies in Autextlac°(π̂): outer automorphisms that send each class of inertia (loop) subgroups attached to x_i to itself, without permuting them.

Page 28 recalled the discrete Dehn–Nielsen–Baer fact. The Teichmüller (mapping class) group Γ_{g,ν} equals the group of outer automorphisms of the discrete surface group that preserve the loop classes and the orientation. This page opens with 'isomorphisme, et dans ces cas on en déduit un [...] au profini'.

Grothendieck then writes a commutative diagram (4) of exact sequences:
- Top row: 1 → π_1(M̄_{g,ν}) → π_1(M_{g,ν}) → Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q) → 1.
- Bottom row: 1 → T̂_{g,ν} → Autextlac°(π̂) → quotient → 1.
- The left vertical arrow π_1(M̄_{g,ν}) = Γ̂_{g,ν} → T̂_{g,ν} carries the mark '≃?'. Here T̂_{g,ν} is the profinite Teichmüller group, viewed inside Autextlac°.

He notes that T̂_{g,ν} is invariant (normal) in Autextlac°(π̂). He would like the central vertical arrow π_1(M_{g,ν}) → Autextlac°(π̂) to be an isomorphism. That would give a purely group-theoretic, 'anabelian' description Γ ≅ Autextlac°(π̂)/T̂_{g,ν}, with a single such description for every hyperbolic (g,ν).

Example (g,ν) = (0,3): T̂_{0,3} is trivial, so this gives Gal(Q̄/Q) ≅ Autextlac°(π_1(P^1∖{0,1,∞})^), the formula 'déjà envisagée'.

The left margin (black, then blue additions) weakens this to a 'conjecture éventuelle': π_1(M_{g,ν};ξ) ≅ the normalizer of T̂_{g,ν} in Autextlac°(π̂). The blue text seems to add 'en admettant que T̂_{g,ν} est ... [commutant?] ... structure', i.e. it may define T̂ by an extra structure. The bottom margin says the case g=0, ν=3 needs more care, probably an additional condition. This echoes p.28's 'je fais une erreur dans le cas g=0, ν=3'.

The next page passes to N_{g,ν} = M_{g,ν}/S_ν. It asks whether Γ → Autext(T̂_{g,ν}) is injective or bijective, and about the automorphism group of M̄_{g,ν}. The purpose throughout is to characterise Gal(Q̄/Q) as an automorphism group of profinite Teichmüller-type objects, i.e. single-level precursors of the Esquisse/Teichmüller-tower programme.
errors: The left vertical arrow Γ̂_{g,ν} → Out(π̂) being an isomorphism onto its image (injectivity) is the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups. This does not follow formally from Dehn–Nielsen–Baer, since profinite completion is not left exact. It is known for g ≤ 2 (Asada; Boggi; also Hoshi–Mochizuki for g=0,1) and is open or disputed in general. Grothendieck's '≃?' correctly flags this as unproven, but 'on en déduit ... au profini' would be a gap.

Normality of T̂_{g,ν} in the full Autextlac°(π̂) is asserted, not proved. If T̂ is defined as the closure of the image of Γ̂_{g,ν}, normality in the whole inertia-preserving outer automorphism group is not evident. The margin's retreat to a 'normalizer' formulation suggests he saw this.

For (g,ν) = (0,3), the claim Gal(Q̄/Q) ≅ Autextlac°(F̂_2) is not known. It is generally expected to be too optimistic: the inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of F̂_2 contain the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT, which already needs the extra 2- and 3-cycle and pentagon relations coming from M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}. This is consistent with the margin notes (p.28 and here) that the case g=0, ν=3 needs further conditions.

The central vertical arrow can only be surjective if Autextlac° normalises T̂. Even then, surjectivity is a strong anabelian statement; for g=0 it is only obtained after passing to configuration spaces or towers (Nakamura; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki).

ideas.what: Outer Galois representation π_1(M_{g,ν}) → Out(π̂_1(X∖{x_i})) with image in inertia-preserving outer automorphisms; exact sequence 1 → Γ̂_{g,ν} → π_1(M_{g,ν}) → G_Q → 1
ideas.modern_name: Universal monodromy / outer Galois representation of the moduli stack (Oda, Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2; letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Question whether Γ̂_{g,ν} → Out(π̂_1 of surface) is an isomorphism onto the profinite Teichmüller group T̂_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Asada (g=0, 2001), Boggi (g=2 and claims), Hoshi–Mochizuki; open in general
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse (profinite Teichmüller tower); not stated explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Conjecture Gal(Q̄/Q) ≅ Autextlac°(π̂)/T̂_{g,ν}, or π_1(M_{g,ν}) ≅ normalizer of T̂_{g,ν} in inertia-preserving Out(π̂), for each hyperbolic (g,ν) separately
ideas.modern_name: Galois–Teichmüller rigidity / anabelian characterisation of G_Q; normalizer theorems (Nakamura's Galois rigidity of pure sphere braid groups; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki Out(π_1(M_{0,n}))≅GT×S_n; Boggi–Funar–Lochak)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, tower form); Drinfeld/Ihara (GT); Nakamura (1990s); Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme: G_Q vs. automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower (tower version, not this single-level version)

ideas.modern_name: Belyi injectivity plus the (open, expected false) bijectivity question; refined by GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of P^1 minus 3 points and GT-type description)

missed.claim: A dated (c.1980–81) pre-Esquisse formulation at a single level (fixed g,ν, not the whole tower): G_Q would be the quotient of the inertia-preserving outer automorphism group of one profinite surface group by the profinite Teichmüller group. In the margin this becomes a normalizer conjecture π_1(M_{g,ν}) ≅ N_{Autextlac°}(T̂_{g,ν}). This is essentially the shape of later 'Galois rigidity' theorems (Nakamura; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki; Boggi–Funar–Lochak), which were proved for configuration spaces or with extra structure. It also shows that Grothendieck already suspected the g=0, ν=3 single-curve version needs extra conditions.
missed.quote: Voudrais conjecture éventuelle: π_1(M_{g,ν};ξ) ≃ normalisateur de T̂_{g,ν} dans Autextlac°(π_1(X∖{x_1…x_ν})^)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The single-level normalizer statement for higher genus (g ≥ 1) is still not settled, as far as I know. It ties together the congruence subgroup problem and anabelian Galois rigidity. Historically, it documents that the GT/Teichmüller-tower picture grew out of an earlier single-surface conjecture that Grothendieck recognised as problematic for (0,3).

missed.claim: The precise extra structure ('commutant ... structure', blue margin) needed to cut T̂_{g,ν} out, and the condition needed in the (0,3) case, are left unspecified.
missed.quote: Pour le cas g=0, ν=3 il conviendrait d'être [plus prudent?] ... d'exiger ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The extra conditions later found (GT relations from M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}) are exactly what Grothendieck seems to be groping for. A specialist might compare his intended condition with GT.

deep.surprise_reason: Not new mathematics relative to Esquisse and the Galois–Teichmüller literature, but it is an early, dated single-level and normalizer formulation that anticipates later rigidity theorems. It also implicitly contains the congruence subgroup question.
transcription_corrections: The diagram is labelled (4) in the left margin, not (*); the next page refers to 'la première ligne de (4)'.
The bottom-right term of the lower row looks like 'Quot...' (a quotient), with a vertical arrow to 1 below it, rather than 'Out(...)'.
The left vertical arrow carries '≃?' (question mark), indicating an open isomorphism, with T̂_{g,ν} written beside it over crossed-out text.
'[...] que T̂_{g,ν} est invariant' is probably 'Notons/Remarquons que T̂_{g,ν} est invariant dans Autextlac°( )'.
'la flèche verticale centrale du (5)' should probably read '(4)'.
The underbrace under Autextlac°(π_1(X∖{x_1…x_ν})^)/T̂_{g,ν} reads something like 'groupe anabélien bien connu?'; uncertain.
The left-margin blue additions appear to read 'en admettant que T̂_{g,ν} ... commutant ... structure ...'; highly uncertain.
